message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released in 1995.

Key characteristics:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform‑independent** | Java code is compiled into bytecode that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), allowing the same program to run on any device with a JVM. |
| **Object‑oriented** | Everything is an object (except primitives), encouraging encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. |
| **Strongly typed** | Types are checked at compile time, reducing runtime errors. |
| **Automatic memory management** | Garbage collector frees developers from manual memory deallocation. |
| **Rich standard library** | Includes utilities for networking, I/O, collections, concurrency, GUI (Swing/JavaFX), and more. |
| **Multithreading support** | Built‑in threading model and high‑level concurrency utilities. |
| **Security** | Sandbox model for applets, bytecode verification, and access control. |

Typical use cases include:

- Enterprise back‑end services (Spring, Jakarta EE)
- Android mobile apps (Java + Kotlin)
- Desktop applications (Swing, JavaFX)
- Embedded systems
- Scientific computing and big data (Hadoop, Spark)

Java’s syntax is similar to C/C++ but with a simpler memory model and a focus on portability and safety. It remains one of the most widely used programming languages worldwide.
